subject: Post-incident closure, assurance notes, and concrete action plan for Luma Health
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@lumahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial RCA draft and proposed actions for Monday incident

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for your patience while we completed the investigation. Attached is our consolidated RCA draft (RCA-Luma-20270428.pdf) and an editable action tracker (luma-action-tracker-20270430.xlsx). This note summarizes the key findings and the immediate customer-facing commitments we propose: 

Summary (TL;DR)
- Incident window: 2027-04-26 10:23 UTC to 2027-04-26 11:48 UTC (service degraded for inference on west-us region).
- Root cause: unbounded memory growth in a cache eviction path triggered by a rare sequence of heavy-batched requests plus a runtime GC interaction.
- Impact: increased latency and 12% request failures for affected model routes for ~85 minutes.

What we are committing to you now
- Technical fixes deployed to prevent the memory regression (hotfix rolled 2027-04-27 03:40 UTC).
- Short-term mitigation: autoscaler policy adjustment and extra capacity in west-us for your reserved pools.
- Long-term: code-level fix to eviction logic + additional chaos tests before canary.

Action items I recommend we share in the customer-facing packet (we can tailor the language):
1) Timeline and concise root cause (one page).
2) Actions taken during the incident (bullet list, timestamps).
3) Remediation plan with owners and estimated completion dates (we propose 30/60/90-day milestones).
4) Assurance artifacts: runbook updates, test reports, and an independent verification window (we propose a 2-week verification period).

Attached for your review. If these commitments look right to you we will send a formal customer closure email tomorrow morning with the attachments and a link to the action tracker in Drive.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
[attachment: RCA-Luma-20270428.pdf (PDF)]
[attachment: luma-action-tracker-20270430.xlsx (Excel)]

-----Original Message-----
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@lumahealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial RCA draft and proposed actions for Monday incident

Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple questions before we finalize the closure note: 

1) Can you quantify how many of our requests failed vs timed out? We need numbers for our internal audit.
2) We need an explicit assurance timeline for the remediation items. Can you translate the 30/60/90 into concrete dates?
3) Will you share the updated runbook and test logs (where in Drive)?

Also want to understand the compensation path you suggested on our earlier call — can you outline next steps there so I can present to procurement?

Appreciate it — Alex
Sr. SRE, Luma Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial RCA draft and proposed actions for Monday incident

Thanks Alex — I pulled numbers and translated timeline items into concrete dates below. I copied the public artifacts into the shared Drive folder (link at end).

Key metrics (Luma Health routes, west-us region)
- Total requests during window: 48,392
- Failed requests (5xx): 5,807 (12.0%)
- Timeouts (client-observed): 1,246 (2.6%)
- Median latency increase from baseline: +620ms

Concrete remediation timeline we will commit to (dates are target completion):
- 2027-04-27: Hotfix deployed to eviction logic (completed 03:40 UTC).
- 2027-05-07: Canary rollout of the tightened cache eviction + additional telemetry (internal canary, 48h).
- 2027-05-21: Full rollout to production across regions (post-canary verification).
- 2027-06-15: Runbook changes and automated chaos tests added to CI.
- 2027-07-01: Independent verification window complete; Redwood will share the verification report and logs.

Owner assignments (initial)
- Hotfix + production monitoring: Jonas Weber (jonas.weber@redwood.ai) — owner for canary rollout and telemetry.
- Runbook and test automation: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.ai).
- Customer communications and verification packet: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.ai).

Compensation pathway (procurement)
- We propose a credit equal to one week of service for the affected routes, applied to your next invoice, pending review from finance. We will provide a formal credit memo once you accept the closure packet.

Drive + verification links
- https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cLuma-RCA
- RCA and action tracker are in the folder; verification report will be added after the independent window.

Next steps
- Kimberly to approve the customer-facing packet language.
- Alex to confirm acceptance of the proposed credit path or propose alternatives.
- Schedule a 30-minute wrap-up call next week (I can coordinate).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Alex / Priya —

Attached is the final customer packet. Highlights:
- RCA (one-page summary) and full timeline (detailed timestamps).
- Concrete remediation calendar with named owners and target dates (see action tracker).
- Immediate relief: one-week service credit offered; finance will prepare the credit memo after your confirmation.

We are scheduling a 30-minute call next week to walk through any remaining questions and the verification plan — Marissa will send calendar options.

Thank you for the partnership and for raising this quickly — we know reliability is critical to your platform.

Sincerely,

Kimberly Park
